items.name: Auto Scaling group
items.explanation: A set of cloud servers managed as one unit. It keeps a chosen number of instances running, replaces unhealthy ones, and adds or removes instances between a minimum and a maximum size that you set.

assumedBy.quote: The large number of broken instances caused us to hit our pre-configured autoscaling-group size limits, which determine the maximum number of instances in our web tier.

items.name: Transit Gateway and VPCs
items.explanation: A VPC is a private network inside a cloud account. A transit gateway is a managed hub that connects many VPCs, so traffic between them flows through it and shares its capacity.

assumedBy.quote: We use AWS Transit Gateways (TGWs) as hubs to link our VPCs.

sources.title: What is AWS Transit Gateway for Amazon VPC?

items.name: The open files limit
items.explanation: Linux caps how many files a process may hold open at once, and network connections count as files. A process that reaches the cap gets errors when it tries to open another.

assumedBy.quote: the most significant one was the Linux open files limit, but we also exceeded an AWS quota limit
